translation.english_title: Until a thousand crescents are seen

english_lines: Until a thousand crescents are seen,
Until the roar of the wave-sea falls still,
O Tamil, for you — you alone, for me,
I shall wait, I shall wait.....
Until fruit-bounty dries up in the world,
Until the wealth of literature lives,
Until the beauty of youth is spent,
Until old age surges into the body,
notes: `தமிழே` remains direct address as `O Tamil`; the lyric's Tamil/beloved doubleness is not flattened into a generic love-song pronoun.
Sun-procession, fruit-bounty, Podhigai breeze, literary wealth, youth and old age remain separate duration images.
The verified source form `பொன்னி நதியான்` is not silently normalized; `nadiyaan` is retained as an explicit pressure point while `Ponni` remains identifiable.
The repeated `காத்திருப்பேன்` and `(ஆயிரம்)` refrain architecture is preserved.

translator_notes: The song binds Tamil-address, landscape, literature, youth and ageing into a vow of waiting; the English preserves that accumulation rather than reducing it to romantic abstraction.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
